questions: Is the ankle swelling painful, red/warm to the touch, or associated with calf pain or shortness of breath?
Is the ankle swelling in both legs *pitting* (does it leave an indentation when you press your thumb on it for 5 seconds)?
Have you had any recent shortness of breath when lying flat or waking up at night gasping for air?
Are you taking any medicines that can cause swelling (especially blood pressure medicines like amlodipine, NSAIDs like ibuprofen, steroids, or hormones such as estrogen)?
Have you noticed any shortness of breath with exertion or waking up at night with breathlessness (even without lying-flat symptoms)?
Is the ankle swelling worse at the end of the day and better overnight (i.e., does it improve after lying down)?
Have you noticed any new swelling of your face or hands, or sudden shortness of breath or wheezing since the swelling began?
Have you had any recent changes in urination (less urine than usual, foamy urine, or dark/bloody urine)?
Have you noticed new shortness of breath when walking up stairs or during exertion, even if you don’t feel short of breath at rest?
When you press your thumb firmly on the swollen ankle for 5 seconds, does it leave a visible indentation (a “pit”) afterward?
answers: Yes, it’s painful—my pain is around 4/10, more like a tugging pain, and I have swelling in both ankles (right more). I don’t know about redness or warmth to the touch, and I don’t have shortness of breath. I’m not sure about calf pain specifically.
I’m not sure if it’s pitting—when I press it, I haven’t noticed an indentation clearly after 5 seconds. It feels swollen, mostly around both ankles.
No, I don’t have shortness of breath, and no symptoms like waking up gasping or trouble when lying flat.
Yes, I’m currently taking anti-inflammatory drugs. I also take a calcium channel blocker (blood pressure medicine). I’m not on any hormones like estrogen, and I’m not taking steroids.
No—I haven’t noticed shortness of breath with walking or any breathlessness at night.
I can’t say it’s worse at the end of the day or clearly better overnight. It just feels like it’s been swollen in both ankles and also the thighs, without a clear pattern.
No—no new swelling in my face or hands, and no sudden shortness of breath or wheezing since the swelling started.
I haven’t noticed any recent changes in urination—no less urine, no foamy urine, and no dark or bloody urine.
No, I don’t have new shortness of breath with stairs or exertion.
I’m not sure—when I press it, I haven’t clearly seen an indentation stay afterward. It feels swollen, but I can’t confirm pitting after 5 seconds.
